title: SHALLOW WATER MINE COUNTERMEASURES
description: Shallow water mine countermeasures and the Shallow Water Assault Breaching System (SABRE), a rocket deployed explosive line charge to detonate mine threats are tested, inert segment flight testing is a short line charge segments of the Mark 22 Mod 4 Rocket Motors, Distributed Explosive Technology (DET) uses an explosive net array to disable mine threat, Breach Line Navigation Project and techniques are shown,  Feb. 1, 1993. (U.S. Navy video)

transcript.text: The shallow water assault breaching system or SABER is a rocket deployed four-and-fifty-foot-long explosive line charge
designed to neutralize and engage in mind threats in the serve zone.
SABER's performance is achieved using discrete ten-pound charges of underwater-based explosives spaced at three-foot intervals.
SABER will use a rear-mounted fire and forget fuse to initiate a detonating cord which runs and lights the system.
System detonation will disable and or detonate various mind threats within its blast zone.
A series of test shots were conducted to optimize explosive charge size and spacing
as well as to determine explosive output and minute utilization effectiveness.
Preliminary flight testing of short-line charge segments are being conducted using the Mark-22 Mod-4 rocket motor.
These tests will be used to optimize the interconnecting strength-member design
and to establish preliminary system flight characteristics.
In these initial tests, safety lines and drug parachutes are used to tether the rocket motor
to compensate for the limited length of line charge being flown.
Another system under development is Distributed Explosive Technology, or DET.
This system utilizes an explosive net array to disable and or detonate various mind threats in the serve zone.
Shown here is subscaled deployment testing of an earlier array of 90-foot width by two-in-foot depth
using two modified Mark-22 Mod-4 rocket motors.
Deployment of this subscale and nerve prototype was conducted to determine system deployment characteristics
for various rocket motor launch angles and asmits.
Efforts are currently ongoing to establish an explosive array configuration of proper detonating cord density
and spacing for optimum performance against serve zone and placed mind threats.
The Breach Lane Navigation Project is currently analyzing and testing various equipment and techniques
that will allow LCAC operators to navigate their craft through previously cleared assault transit lanes.
One of the methods being considered for lane navigation is to utilize a beach-and-placed directional light source
which will allow LCAC operators to move their craft onto the same bearing line as that projected by the light source.
Here we see LCAC personnel from a cross-assolved craft unit 5 using a color-projected light source
to establish their position relative to the center of the desired transit lane and to provide them with the course correction data.
In support of the shallow water mine-kind of measures programs, the Rice-Pettie test target at Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
is being refurbished to accommodate the testing of all anticipated explosive neutralization systems.
Shown here under construction is the test basin which is used for explosive performance testing
and a reservoir to accommodate the draining and filling of the basin between test shots.
A synthetic liner and geoweb matting are installed in both the test basin and reservoir for water retention and erosion control.
Eventually the test basin will be backfilled with 20 feet of sand to establish a blast buffer between charges
in place on the bottom of the basin and the underlining synthetic liner.
